You are grading text generated by a language model running on quantized hardware. Quantization damages a model in characteristic ways — corrupted tokens, repeated words, foreign script leaking into English — and your job is to say how damaged this response is. Ordinary weaknesses count too, but far less than corruption.

Rate the response from 0 to 10. Any integer is allowed. The bands:

0 — Empty, or so garbled it does not read as language.

1-3 — A decoding failure. Any one of: junk or nonsense tokens ("pep-e-e-e-e", "10-15-15-15-15"); mojibake or broken encoding ("Saut?", "pur ed" for "puréed", "68-72?F"); non-English script dropped into an English sentence; a degenerate loop repeating until the token limit; the same sentence or paragraph restated almost verbatim several times; text truncated mid-sentence or starting mid-sentence. These are the worst thing a response can have: one clear instance belongs in this band even if everything else about the response is excellent.

4-6 — Fluent, well-formed English with no decoding failure, but a real flaw. Any one of: a duplicated word or short phrase that a reader reads straight past ("trained on large datasets, datasets, and evaluated on held-out data"); a dangling "**" or a header with no closing marker; a misspelling ("constanty", "Frittatta"); code with a syntax error or a call to a function that was never defined; a blatant factual or arithmetic error (Newton born in 1492, a sum that is wrong, a unit conversion off by 1000x). One such flaw is about 5.

A duplicated word is the mildest flaw in this band — the sentence still reads correctly and the meaning survives — so rate it 5 or 6. It only drops into 1-3 if the duplication keeps happening, at which point it is a loop rather than a stumble.

7-9 — Fluent, accurate English with no decoding failure and no blatant error. Come down into this band for reasoning that does not hold up: an unsupported leap, a conclusion that does not follow from the argument, an analogy that breaks down, a self-contradiction, or padding that avoids answering. Clearly shaky logic is about 7; a small nitpick is 9.

10 — No issues. Coherent, fluent, accurate, and it answers what was asked.

Do not be nitpicky. These are NOT flaws: style, tone, verbosity, redundant section headers, emoji, formatting taste, hedging, or a response being shorter than you would have written. A translation request answered in the target language is correct, not foreign script. Punctuation inside or outside quotes and bold markers is not a defect.

Write at most two short sentences saying what is wrong, or that nothing is. Then give the rating on its own line, in exactly this format:

Rating: [[N]]

Commit to one rating even if you are torn. Do not restart your analysis or argue with yourself.
